The Encore Is a Beastly Truck Camper With All the Luxury, Now for Sale for an Eye-Watering Price
63 photos
Photo: Rossmonster
I've seen few truck camper builds that are as extensive and adventure-ready as those from Rossmonster. Today, I'm checking out a "pre-loved and pre-built" rig, as it calls them, that's looking for a new owner – I'll tell you more about pricing at the end of the article so as not to shock you straight away.
Meet Encore, a project that's based on a 2025 Ram 5500 Crew Cab with a 4x4 drive. As I mentioned, it was created by Rossmonster, a Longmont, Colorado-based company that transforms trucks and vans into incredibly capable homes on wheels.
When it comes to truck campers, Rossmonster offers two options: the Baja Trail and the better-equipped Baja Plus – the Encore is, as expected given how it looks, part of the latter category.
The company made sure to make the Encore trail-ready – and not just fit for simple trails, but also for more hardcore off-roading. The stock Ram 5500 can already handle going off the beaten path – this one is powered by a 6.7-liter Cummins turbo diesel engine outputting around 360 hp and 800 lb-ft. (1,084 Nm) of torque.
However, the builders added all the right options to improve the off-road capability. First off, the vehicle rides on 20-inch raw aluminum wheels wrapped in Michelin X Force ZL rough-terrain tires.
Photo: Rossmonster I also love how this wheel and tire combo fits in aesthetically, with the aluminum rims pairing nicely with the blue vehicle body and the grey camper box. The camper box is a custom composite frame sitting over an aluminum frame. Furthermore, the entire vehicle is coated in Raptor truck bed liner for an extra layer of protection.
Second, the truck is equipped with a Liquid Springs suspension – it's a fully active, smart hydraulic suspension system that replaces a truck's factory leaf springs, coil springs, and shock absorbers.
Instead, it uses a compressible silicon fluid combined with computer microprocessors to dynamically alter the truck's spring rate and damping in real time, 1,000 times per second. It also has a Tru-Earth Leveling system, which levels the truck automatically by adjusting each hydraulic strut on its own.
At the front, you'll come across two ditch lights and a massive Hammerhead bumper complete with D-Ring recovery points, a Warn winch rated for 20,000 lb. (9,071 kg), and an integrated Baja Designs clear LED light strip.
Photo: Rossmonster On the opposite end, there are additional useful accessories: a spare tire carrier and two carriers holding cargo boxes with adjustable shelving and Molle panels on the side. Underneath, you'll discover a custom Rossmonster Baja bumper with a backup camera, Rigid scene lights, an ARB air compressor, and a hitch receiver.
I saved the most significant exterior mod for last: a gigantic elevating roof. At the touch of a button, you can raise the camper box's roof to create a ton of additional room inside. By doing this, you'll also reveal several windows. When you're driving, it stays low to reduce height, improve clearance, and minimize wind resistance.
Rossmonster put the roof space to great use. It installed four solar panels with a total capacity of 760 W, a Fiamma awning, two Maxxair vent fans, and a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit.
Before we take a look inside, I wanted to mention that Rossmonster even put the cab to good use. It removed the rear passenger seat arrangement and replaced it with a storage platform providing multiple compartments. Moreover, it added a 4-camera system and a Garmin screen for navigation. A nice touch is that a door lets you pass from the cabin to the living space and vice-versa.
Photo: Rossmonster Other notable exterior mods are traction boards attached on the passenger side, a large Molle panel, running boards for the cab that have integrated hammock pole mounts, powered steps for the camper box, and power and water connections.
The contrast between the exterior and the interior couldn't be more drastic – you move from a rugged exterior to a warm and welcoming interior packed with luxuries.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice walls upholstered in grey tweed fabric, white oak slab-door cabinets, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by white Corian Platinum solid-surface countertops, black leather upholstery for the seats, and a custom topo backsplash (topo as in it imitates the pattern of topographic maps).
Dead ahead as you enter, Rossmonster created one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: a bathroom. Hidden behind a conventional white oak door, it boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a Thetford cassette toilet, a teak floor insert, and a removable hanging rack.
Photo: Rossmonster Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features an Isotherm Cruise 200 stainless steel fridge with a freezer compartment, a two-burner induction stovetop, a microwave oven, a deep sink with a folding faucet and a cutting board cover, and a multi-function Panasonic oven. Counter space is arguably quite limited, but you get two flip-up tables that create more surface area.
On the opposite side, you'll come across a massive storage unit. It offers three large drawers, a pull-out pantry, a small counter, and a huge fridge/freezer.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by a lounge area. It has a U-shaped couch and a large table in the middle. You can drop the table to the same height as the couch, rearrange the cushions, and transform this area into a comfy sleeping arrangement for the guests.
Several overhead cabinets follow the same shape as the couch and provide plenty of room for storage. What's more, above, the builders fitted a Maxxair vent fan.
Photo: Rossmonster Three benches make up the couch. Besides offering a bit more space to store your items, they accommodate the utility systems.
The electrical system's highlights are a 1,200 Ah battery bank paired with a 3,000 W inverter/charger. Three charging sources are available: solar power, shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the rig is equipped with a 40-gallon (151-liter) freshwater tank, an additional 25-gallon (95-liter) freshwater tank underneath the vehicle, an under-mounted greywater tank, and a single-stage water filtration system.
The last important systems in this rig are a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit and a Rixen's MCS7 hydronic heating system that provides heated air and hot water. It also powers a radiant floor heating system.
Photo: Rossmonster You'll have to use a ladder by the rig's entrance to get into the bedroom, which is located above the driver's cabin. This is undoubtedly a comfier solution compared to the rear sleeping arrangement. It also has a Maxxair vent fan above, two reading lights, and two front-facing windows.
As I said initially, the Encore is now for sale . You'll need a fortune to be able to get your hands on it - $440,000 (€393,580), to be precise, as shared on its listing. It currently has 16,889 miles (27,180 km).
You could get a conventional house for that money, so it's only fair that some people will have a strong reaction to this price tag.
However, it's safe to assume that the target audience for such a creation won't be bound by a budget. And it's undeniable that this truck camper by Rossmonster is an awesome adventure machine that can take you off-road and keep you off-grid for long periods.
